entities.summary:
Cleopatra Selene II was the last active ruler of the Ptolemaic Kingdom, reigning as Queen of Cyrenaica and Queen of Mauretania alongside her husband Juba II from 40 BCE until her death in 4 BCE. She was a member of the Ptolemaic dynasty, which was a Greek dynasty that ruled Egypt after the death of Alexander the Great. Born into a wealthy and influential family, Cleopatra Selene II was educated in the traditional skills of a Ptolemaic princess, including music, poetry, and diplomacy. She married Juba II, the king of Numidia, in 40 BCE, and the two ruled together until Juba II's death in 20 BCE. After Juba II's death, Cleopatra Selene II became the sole ruler of Cyrenaica, and she worked to maintain the stability and prosperity of her kingdom. She was known for her intelligence, courage, and diplomatic skills, and she played a key role in maintaining the peace and stability of the Mediterranean region. 

The death of Cleopatra Selene II in 4 BCE marked the end of the Ptolemaic Kingdom, and it paved the way for the Roman Empire to expand its territories in Egypt. Her legacy continued to be felt in the region for centuries, and she remains one of the most famous and influential women of the ancient world.

Cleopatra Selene II's reign was marked by a series of significant events, including the Roman conquest of Egypt, the Ptolemaic dynasty's decline, and the rise of the Roman Empire. She was a key figure in the transition from the Ptolemaic to the Roman period, and her legacy continues to be studied by historians today.

Cleopatra Selene II's significance extends beyond her own reign, as she played a key role in shaping the course of Mediterranean history. Her diplomatic skills, intelligence, and courage helped to maintain the peace and stability of the region, and her legacy continues to be felt today. She remains one of the most fascinating and influential women of the ancient world, and her story continues to captivate historians and scholars around the world.
